poc_summary: /poc/poc.c + /poc/run.sh: builds an X509 with a valid past notBefore and a crafted notAfter ASN1_STRING whose data buffer is set via ASN1_STRING_set0() to an OPENSSL_malloc(5) buffer containing "99991" (a byte-for-byte, non-NUL-terminated prefix of the magic string "99991231235959Z"). run.sh compiles poc.c against the built /work/libcrypto.a and libssl.a (with matching ASan/UBSan flags) and calls the internal ossl_x509_check_cert_time(ctx, x, -1) directly (declared via crypto/x509/x509_local.h), driving the vulnerable strcmp() to read past the 5-byte heap allocation. Run identically via run_poc on pre_intro, post_intro, post_benign.
explanation: meta.json/discussion.md: intro commit 3c963394d0c7 (parent 48a2d1e448d4) added a "99991231235959Z" no-expiry special case to ossl_x509_check_cert_time() in crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c that calls strcmp() on the raw ASN1_STRING_get0_data() buffer of the notAfter field, which is not guaranteed to be NUL-terminated. Upstream fix dfc6f643c09a (mirrored by post_benign) replaces this with an explicit length check (`notafter->length == 15`) plus memcmp(). Source diff confirms: pre_intro has none of this special-case code at all; post_intro has the strcmp version; post_benign has the length-checked memcmp version. Because normal DER-parsed X.509 certs are always NUL-terminated in this non-fuzzing build configuration (no-fuzz-libfuzzer/no-fuzz-afl; ASN1_STRING_set()/asn1_collect() both append a NUL byte unless FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION is defined), no ordinary certificate-parsing path can supply a non-NUL-terminated buffer here, matching the upstream report title "heap-buffer-overflow in CI fuzzing tests". I therefore built a minimal harness that calls the internal function directly with a controlled ASN1_STRING (via the public ASN1_STRING_set0() API) holding an exactly-sized, non-NUL-terminated buffer that is a genuine prefix of the magic string (so strcmp does not mismatch before running off the end of the allocation) — this reaches the exact vulnerable line via the real target code path (ossl_x509_check_cert_time), not a source copy or grep. Running the identical run.sh/poc.c through run_poc against all three built revisions: pre_intro exits cleanly (return 0, no crash — code doesn't exist yet), post_intro crashes under AddressSanitizer with "heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 6 ... in __interceptor_strcmp ... in ossl_x509_check_cert_time /work/crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c:2213" (the exact strcmp line added by the intro commit, 0 bytes past a 5-byte CRYPTO_malloc'd region), and post_benign exits cleanly again (return 0) using the length-checked memcmp fix. This satisfies the invariance requirement (identical reproducer across all three revisions) with an unambiguous, target-specific sanitizer report confined to post_intro only.

oracle.description: AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow report naming the exact vulnerable line (x509_vfy.c:2213, the strcmp on ASN1_STRING_get0_data(notafter) added by the intro commit) fires only on post_intro under run_poc; pre_intro and post_benign both complete normally (exit=0, "ossl_x509_check_cert_time returned 0 / DONE_NO_CRASH") for the identical harness/input.
